rationale: Round 7: reviews the three small, uncommitted hunks that fix the branch-6 round's CR-001 (dirty.py's _SPAN_HOOK_TYPES missing agent.tool.denied) and CR-002 (two misleading tests that claimed to prove real-hook behaviour but only seeded a hand-crafted session_dims row). All three lenses ran to completion. The blind lens found no new correctness issues and confirmed the two previously-fixed bugs (empty-NOT-IN spend_sessions guard, missing NULLS LAST) are still present; its two notes (an undocumented sum-vs-count NULL-propagation invariant, and no run evidence for make test-cli-analytics-live visible from the diff alone) are non-blocking observations, not defects. The edge-case lens confirmed the dirty.py fix is correct and complete -- the separate _is_finished_dispatch cross-midnight sub-gate deliberately excludes agent.tool.denied (verified against fork_attribution.py's _ended_call and rollups.py's _FINISHED_DISPATCH_HOOK, both of which independently confirm a denied call never gets an end/error hook, so there is nothing for that sub-gate to re-match) -- and that _SPAN_HOOK_TYPES has exactly one consumer, so the widening has no side effect. It also confirmed test_dirty.py's two edited parametrize lists are generic over event_type and genuinely exercise the new value, and that every other agent.tool.error allowlist in src/ already includes agent.tool.denied (no missed fourth gate). It found one real, concrete defect in my own CR-002 fix: _seed_via_hooks never set hook_events.user_email, so the two reseeded tests' session_dims ended up with jwt_email/dev_name_max/developer_name all NULL, and seed.window()'s users=[self.email] filter then excluded the session by email mismatch alone -- a vacuous pass that proved nothing about the actual admission/exclusion logic CR-002 was about. I independently verified this (confirmed hook_events has a user_email column read by the dims upsert at rollups.py:1987, and that reader.py's _filter_conditions applies lower(user_email) = ANY($users) whenever f.users is set) and fixed it in this same round: _seed_via_hooks now takes an optional user_email parameter, and both edited tests pass seed.email, matching what the replaced seed.dims(...) call provided. The acceptance lens flagged AC4 as partial for a related but distinct reason: the existing live test test_a_tool_denied_hook_with_no_successful_call_counts_as_activity (not touched by this round) calls refresher.mark_dirty() with its default _ALL_BITS mask, which goes through the _MARK_RANGE/_FALLBACK_HOOKS backfill-path SQL, not dirty.py's dirty_keys()/_SPAN_HOOK_TYPES -- so no live-Postgres test exercises the specific live-ingest code path this round's fix targets. I investigated this and judge it adequately covered by the existing test architecture rather than a live gap: dirty_keys()'s classification of agent.tool.denied is now directly unit-tested (test_dirty.py, this round), and the ingest-time wiring from ingest_hook_events() to dirty_keys() to a rollup_dirty INSERT with the correct bitmask is already covered by pre-existing, unchanged tests in test_ingestor.py (e.g. test_a_skill_call_end_queues_its_forks_own_day, which captures the real SQL dirty_keys() produces via a FakeEngine). The remaining step -- that a SPAN_FACTS-dirty day actually produces a tool_facts_daily row for a denied-only call -- is proven by the live test via the backfill path, which shares the same, now-consistent _FALLBACK_HOOKS allowlist. No single test proves the full chain end-to-end through the real ingestor against live Postgres, but the composition of unit + mocked-ingestor + live-backfill tests proves every link, so I triage this as a documented test-architecture gap (defer), not a blocker, rather than writing a new live end-to-end ingest test under a 'do it fast' constraint. Standards review passed: all commit subjects in the branch range follow the EPMCDME-16496: <Description> format; the new/changed code stays within its existing module's responsibility and introduces no new injection surface (hardcoded event-type literals only).
